title: I was sent to perfect character
hookLine: the Prophet ﷺ said he was sent to perfect good character

cards: Ask a room why a prophet is sent, and the answers come fast. To bring a law. To call people to worship one God.
To warn, to give good news. All of those are in the Qur'an. But in one hadith the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, sums up his mission in a way that can catch a listener off guard.
Not with law, not with ritual. With character.

teach.b: The word is akhlaq: character, manners, the settled habits of a person, how they are when nobody's grading them.

teach.h: SENT TO PERFECT, NOT TO INVENT.
teach.b: The hadith comes in Imam Malik's Muwatta, among other collections, and in paraphrase it says: I was sent to perfect good character. Imam Ahmad's collection has a version that says noble character. Notice the verb.
Some readers take it to mean that good character, honesty, generosity, keeping a promise, was already known, and the Prophet came to bring it to completion.
The Qur'an says of his own, in Pickthall's translation: "And lo! thou art of a tremendous nature."
And when his wife Aisha was asked to describe his character, her answer in Sahih Muslim is short: his character was the Qur'an. What the book says, he was. So this block turns.
The last block asked what Muslims believe. This one asks what kind of person belief makes.
Muslim scholars wrote whole works on akhlaq: on patience and anger, envy and generosity, the heart's diseases and cures, and we'll walk through some of them.

teach.h: THE BEST OF YOU: BEST IN CHARACTER.
teach.b: A hadith in Bukhari puts the measure plainly: the best of you are those who are best in character. Not the loudest, not the most learned.
A measure anybody can be held to, at a checkout counter, on a crowded train, in a group chat.

how: Muslims study akhlaq, good character, as part of the faith, often starting from the hadith that the Prophet was sent to perfect good character and from accounts of his own conduct.

o: a polite greeting said when entering someone's home
the written rules of Islamic law for daily life
character: the settled habits a person shows every day

s: the hadith says the Prophet was sent to invent good character
it says perfect: bring to completion, not invent.
Aisha described the Prophet's character as the Qur'an
her answer, in Sahih Muslim, is that his character was the Qur'an.
in Bukhari, the best people are measured by their character
the hadith says the best of you are those best in character.

games.q: someone asks Aisha to describe his character. what does she say?
o: she lists his habits one by one.
she says it can't be described.
games.why: her answer is short: what the book says, he was.

practice: Pick one trait you'd like to grow, patience, honesty, generosity, gentleness, keeping your word, and shrink it to something small enough to do before tonight: one true sentence where an easy one would do, letting someone go first, the call you said you'd make.
Say that small act to yourself, plainly, once. If you pray, ask Allah to beautify your character in your own words; if not, simply set the intention.

wordCard.voice: Akhlaq. Character: the settled habits of a person, which the Prophet said he was sent to perfect. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: character, manners; the plural of khuluq.

carryVoice: Your line: sent for character. Good character wasn't invented; he came to perfect it. Until tomorrow.
